Sur le Danube, certaines centrales serbes ne fonctionnent plus qu’à 20 % de leur capacité. Pour en parler, Roger Spautz, chargé de campagne nucléaire chez Greenpeace France et Luxembourg, est l'invité de France 24.

france24fr.title: Birmanie : l’ancienne dirigeante détenue a rencontré la Croix-Rouge
france24fr.description: Maintenue en détention depuis le coup d’État militaire de 2021, l’ancienne dirigeante birmane Aung San Suu Kyi a rencontré des représentants du Comité international de la Croix-Rouge. Récit de Julien Dubois.

france24fr.title: Sécheresse en Serbie : le Danube à un niveau historique, les centrales hydroélectriques menacées
france24fr.description: Le niveau du Danube est tombé à des seuils historiques en Serbie, conséquence de la sécheresse et des fortes chaleurs qui frappent l’Europe depuis des semaines. Récit de Lou Kisiela et Peter O'Brien.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : les incendies de Spokane forcent des évacuations massives
france24fr.description: Dans l’État de Washington, des incendies attisés par des vents violents ont frappé la région de Spokane, entraînant des ordres d’évacuation pour environ 60 000 personnes et détruisant ou endommageant au moins 600 bâtiments. Récit d'Alexandra Quarini.

france24fr.title: 🇲🇦 Maroc : l'angoisse des parents sans nouvelles de leurs enfants passés à Ceuta
france24fr.description: À Fnideq, ville marocaine frontalière de Ceuta, des dizaines de proches se rassemblent le long du grillage barrant l'accès à la mer, dans l'attente de nouvelles de leurs proches, passés illégalement dans l'enclave espagnole.

france24fr.title: Art et protection du vivant : des sculptures contre les chalutiers en Italie
france24fr.description: Vous avez déjà entendu parler de la Casa dei Pesci, la "maison des poissons", en Italie ? Au départ, il y a le combat solitaire de Paolo Fanciulli, un artisan pêcheur révolté par la destruction des océans. Au fil des années, il a fédéré autour de lui des artistes comme Emily Young ou Maurizio Cattelan. Ensemble, ils ont bâti un musée sous-marin qui défend concrètement le vivant. Un barrage contre la surpêche et la bataille d’une vie.

france24fr.title: Cuba au bord du gouffre, le pari de Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Après le Venezuela et l'Iran, Cuba est-elle la prochaine cible dans le viseur de Donald Trump ?Alors que l'île traverse sa pire crise depuis des décennies, Washington durcit le ton et multiplie les sanctions.Est-ce une simple posture politique, ou une véritable stratégie de la part du président américain ? Jusqu'où les États-Unis sont-ils prêts à aller ?Dans cette vidéo, on décrypte les enjeux géopolitiques et les scénarios possibles autour de l’île communiste pour comprendre ce qui se joue à se

france24fr.title: Mégafeux en France : quelle stratégie pour éteindre le feu ?
france24fr.description: Face aux mégafeux qui ravagent la Gironde et le Var, quelles sont les stratégies déployées pour les éteindre ? Reportage de M.Martel, Y.Relat, V.Chatelier (France 2).

france24fr.title: Ceuta : Rabat sort de son silence et annonce 11 morts, l'Espagne en dénombre 72
france24fr.description: La tragédie de Ceuta prend un tournant diplomatique : alors que le Maroc officialise un bilan de 11 morts, l'Espagne en recense 72. Pourquoi cette disparité ? Analyse de Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: Incendies dans le Var : situation sous contrôle, mais les sinistrés restent craintifs
france24fr.description: En France, les feux sont désormais globalement maîtrisés. Dans le Var cependant, les habitants et sinistrés restent méfiants face au risque de reprise des flammes. Reportage de R.Radenac et A.Metais (France 2).

france24fr.title: Incendies en Grèce : plus de 12 000 hectares ravagés en une semaine
france24fr.description: En une semaine, plus de 12 000 hectares de forêts et de terres agricoles ont brûlé en Grèce. Le pays traverse ses "jours les plus difficiles" a martelé le porte-parole des pompiers. Récit de Matthieu Bellini (France 2).

france24fr.title: Sahara occidental : une autoroute rebaptisée Trump par Mohammed VI
france24fr.description: Sur décision du roi Mohammed VI, le Maroc a donné le nom du président américain Donald Trump à une autoroute reliant le sud du pays au territoire disputé du Sahara occidental, revendiqué par les indépendantistes sahraouis, a annoncé l'agence officielle marocaine MAP samedi.

france24fr.title: En Sicile, des vacanciers découvrent près de 700 000 euros en billets sur une plage
france24fr.description: Sur une plage de Casuzze, en Sicile, des vacanciers ont découvert des sacs contenant d’importantes liasses de billets, échoués après l’intervention des garde-côtes auprès d’un bateau en difficulté. Le montant retrouvé est estimé à près de 700 000 euros, selon les autorités italiennes, qui ont ouvert une enquête sur l’origine de cette somme. (France 2)

france24fr.title: Fifa : le président Infantino poussé vers la sortie ?
france24fr.description: Gianni Infantino fait face à une contestation grandissante au sein de la Fifa. Après la fronde de l’UEFA et du Concacaf contre son projet d’ouverture du capital lié au Mondial, la pression s’est accentuée sur le président de l’instance, accusé par ces organisations de mauvaise gouvernance et de manque de transparence. Récit de Julien Dubois.

france24fr.title: Brésil : le président brésilien a été investi par son parti et vise un quatrième mandat
france24fr.description: Le président brésilien Lula a été investi par son parti et se lance dans la course à un quatrième mandat. Correspondance de Gustavo Ribeiro depuis São Paulo pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Incendies en France : les pompiers suffisamment protégés ?
france24fr.description: Les incendies se multiplient en France et, avec eux, l’exposition aux fumées toxiques, dont les effets sur la santé peuvent être graves. Les soldats du feu sont-ils suffisamment protégés contre ces fumées chargées de particules fines et de gaz irritants ? (France 2)

france24fr.title: Expulsion de Xenia Fedorova : la justice rejette le recours de la chroniqueuse prorusse
france24fr.description: Le recours de la chroniqueuse prorusse Xenia Fedorova contre son expulsion du territoire a été rejeté lundi matin. L’ex-dirigeante de RT France, assignée depuis mercredi à résidence, n'a démontré aucune "extrême urgence", a justifié le tribunal administratif de Paris.

france24fr.title: Japon et États-Unis unissent leurs forces pour enrayer la chute historique du yen
france24fr.description: Washington et Tokyo ont confirmé être intervenus conjointement sur le marché des changes pour soutenir le yen, tombé à son plus bas niveau face au dollar depuis 1986. Une opération exceptionnelle, motivée à la fois par des enjeux économiques japonais, des intérêts commerciaux américains et la volonté de préserver la stabilité financière. Explications.

zeit.description: Der neue Bundesverkehrsminister Steffen Bilger will die 500 Milliarden Euro Sondervermögen zügig verbauen. Er hält es für sinnvoll, private Partner einzubeziehen.

zeit.description: Die Uefa prüft rechtliche Schritte gegen den Fifa-Chef. Wales entzieht als erster Verband Infantino die Unterstützung für seine Wiederwahl, England plant wohl dasselbe.

zeit.title: Sparkassen-Einbruch in Gelsenkirchen: Polizei führt dreißig Schließfachbesitzer zwangsweise vor
zeit.description: Nach dem Sparkassen-Einbruch in Gelsenkirchen greift die Staatsanwaltschaft durch. Dreißig Schließfachbesitzer müssen zu angeordneten Vernehmungen zwangsweise erscheinen.

zeit.title: Autismus: Treffen sich zwei Autistinnen
zeit.description: Bei Frauen wird Autismus oft spät erkannt, sie maskieren ihn. Hier erzählen zwei von Tanzkurs, Sex und Depressionen. Vom Gefühl, ein Alien zu sein – und was dagegen half.

zeit.title: Pharmaunternehmen: Guido Oelkers wird neuer Chef von BioNTech
zeit.description: Guido Oelkers übernimmt die Nachfolge von BioNTech-Gründer Uğur Şahin. Dieser will den Impfstoffhersteller zusammen mit Co-Gründerin Özlem Türeci bis Ende 2026 verlassen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Iran und Oman verhandeln über Schifffahrtskorridor +++ Trump kündigt für heute neue Gespräche mit Iran an
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Die Feuerwehr in Griechenland kämpft westlich von Athen weiter gegen Waldbrände
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Die neuesten Meldungen über Hitzerekorde, Dürren und Brände in Europa.

nzz.title: Verblüffender U-Turn in der Transfersaga um Vinzenz Rohrer: Statt zum HC Davos wechselt der Stürmer nach Zug

nzz.title: Premiumpreis für die Parklücke: Smart #2 zielt auf die Zielgruppe der Städter, aber nicht auf Schnäppchenjäger
nzz.description: Nach bald dreissig Jahren feierte in China der Smart Fortwo sein Comeback. Doch Europa gibt bei diesem Projekt den Ton an – und wird zum wichtigsten Markt.

nzz.title: Touristenmaschine stürzt in Peru ab – 13 Insassen kommen ums Leben, darunter zwei deutsche Touristen
nzz.description: Ein touristischer Flug endetet tödlich: Unter den Opfern sollen laut ersten Erkenntnissen auch Deutsche sein. Mit demselben Flugzeugtyp kam es in jüngster Zeit bereits zu mehreren schweren Unfällen.

nzz.title: Erstmals seit 15 Jahren: Japan und die USA intervenieren gemeinsam am Devisenmarkt und treiben den Yen-Kurs in die Höhe
nzz.description: Beide Länder drohen mit weiteren Interventionen. Selbst US-Präsident Trump deutet Hilfe für Japan an. Die abrupte Wende drückt auf die Aktienkurse.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

observador.title: Os demónios de Charli — e mais 4 álbuns que levamos de julho
observador.description: Não é fácil nem é comum, mas Charli XCX também não: 1 anos depois do verão "BRAT", um regresso inesperado, mas coerente na surpresa. Foi um dos picos de um mês com diferentes temperaturas.

observador.title: Invasão de Ceuta é um aviso para toda a Europa? — Debate
observador.description: O mar de pessoas que inundou Ceuta não criou só um problema para Espanha. A Europa é agora forçada a discutir a proteção das fronteiras externas e a coesão das políticas de receção aos imigrantes.

observador.title: E tudo o que Trump diz, o Irão desmente
observador.description: O presidente dos EUA anunciou um novo período de negociações a começar esta segunda-feira, mas a diplomacia iraniana já desmentiu. Teerão diz também que ainda não há acordo com Omã sobre Ormuz.

observador.title: Pogacar regressa à Vuelta sete anos depois com Almeida e Ivo
observador.description: Depois de ter sido terceiro em 2019, Pogacar está de volta à Vuelta para fechar a trilogia das Grandes Voltas. Esloveno tem em João Almeida o seu grande apoio, Ivo Oliveira é a aposta para os sprints.

observador.title: Benfica pode cruzar com Aarhus ou Sabah no playoff
observador.description: Benfica ficou a conhecer possíveis adversários no playoff da Liga Europa em caso de vitória na terceira pré-eliminatória frente ao Hearts. Ronda decisiva de apuramento será jogada a 20 e 27 de agosto.

observador.title: 12h. De 60 mil migrantes, continuam em Ceuta perto de 5 mil
observador.description: Número avançado pelo presidente da cidade autónoma, que critica ainda a atuação do Governo de Pedro Sánchez. Ainda, Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros do Irão diz que não há negociações com os EUA.

observador.title: Chefe militar diz que EUA não deixará dominar Indo-Pacífico
observador.description: Samuel Paparo afirmou que alguns países recorrem a "falsas alegações de legitimidade" para justificar ações de intimidação e coerção, em contexto de tensões no mar do Sul da China.

observador.title: Dinamarqueses com serviço militar obrigatório de 11 meses
observador.description: O Exército expandiu o serviço militar devido ao facto de as ameaças e a segurança estarem mais dinâmicas e complexas do que nunca. Os recrutas passarão os primeiros 5 meses a receber formação básica.

observador.title: Évora. Homem que agrediu mulher na via pública em preventiva
observador.description: O homem foi detido por agentes da PSP, em flagrante delito, na sexta-feira. O Ministério Público suspeita que os maus-tratos se sucedem desde o início do relacionamento amoroso.

observador.title: Anna Wintour escolhe John Galliano como tema da Met Gala
observador.description: O polémico designer, que depois de fazer comentários antissemitas em 2011 viu a sua carreira na moda arruinada, prepara um regresso há anos. Agora consagra-se com a ajuda da amiga de longa data.

observador.title: AstraZeneca negoceia fusão com Bristol Myers Squibb
observador.description: Uma eventual fusão seria uma das maiores operações do setor farmacêutico de sempre. A AstraZeneca está avaliada em 264.000 milhões de dólares, já a Bristol Myers Squibb em 133.000 milhões de dólares.

observador.title: O caso da depressão que escondia outra doença
observador.description: O psiquiatra Rui Albuquerque recorda o caso de uma mulher diagnosticada com depressão mas que que, afinal, tinha demência. O objetivo deixou de ser tratar e passou a ser cuidar da pessoa.

observador.title: China. Central nuclear afetada durante tufão Noul
observador.description: Os circuitos A e B das linhas de transmissão Taichong de 500 quilovolts sofreram, sucessivamente, avarias súbitas. A central respondeu, no entanto, de forma estável e eficaz durante o impacto.

observador.title: Teerão nega existência de negociações com os EUA
observador.description: "Não estamos a negociar com os Estados Unidos neste momento. Estamos a negociar com Omã para garantir a passagem pelo Estreito de Ormuz", diz porta-voz do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros do Irão.

observador.title: A crise de Ceuta e as narrativas badaladas pelas redes
observador.description: Pedro Silva Pereira e Carlos Coelho analisam o caos migratório vivido nos últimos dias em Ceuta. Desde as políticas espanholas à conivência marroquina, passado pelas redes sociais, de quem é a culpa?

observador.description: Sismo, a 10 quilómetros de profundidade, foi registado numa zona não habitada na província do Suez. Crescente Vermelho egípcio relata danos em alguns edifícios.

observador.description: Inspeção-Geral da Educação e Ciência detetou várias irregularidades na admissão de estudantes em três cursos da área da Saúde. Universidade criou mecanismo para beneficiar ex-alunos.

observador.title: 10h. Ceuta. Cidade vai voltando à normalidade
observador.description: Enviada especial em Ceuta adianta que maior parte dos imigrantes que ainda se encontram na cidade não são marroquinos. Ainda, Irão desmente Donald Trump e diz não estar em negociações com os E.U.A.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

phys-org.title: Australia has long relied on volunteers: As bird flu spreads, they will need support
phys-org.description: Australia had years to prepare for the arrival of bird flu. The deadly, highly transmissible H5N1 strain emerged in late 2020 in Asia before spreading to every other continent except Australia.

phys-org.title: At colleges, the AI boom means everyone wants to dabble in computer science
phys-org.description: With no background in coding, Faith Maeba, a psychology major, was reluctant when her mother first suggested she enroll in classes on artificial intelligence.

phys-org.title: How digital interferences shape parent-child time
phys-org.description: New research is giving children a voice in understanding how technological interruptions affect parent-child relationships. A paper, "Distracted, Interrupted, or Disrupted: A Pathway Model of Technoference," led by Associate Professor Cara Swit from Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury's (UC) School of Health Sciences, explores how technologies such as smartphones can interfere with parent-child interactions.

phys-org.title: Life speaks one universal language to activate genes: It speaks many more to silence them
phys-org.description: The signals that cells use to switch genes on have remained almost unchanged across 2 billion years of evolution, but the ones used to switch genes off vary dramatically from one branch of life to another, according to a new study from the Center for Genomic Regulation (CRG) in Barcelona.

phys-org.title: South Korea records its highest-ever temperature of 42.5 C
phys-org.description: South Korea registered its highest temperature since records began more than a century ago on Sunday, as authorities warned people to "immediately" stop all outdoor activities in affected areas.

phys-org.title: August's total solar eclipse will sweep over Spain, Iceland and Greenland
phys-org.description: For the first time in more than a century, a total solar eclipse is coming to mainland Spain with an even longer encore next summer.

phys-org.title: How fitness, speed and position shape competition in expanding populations
phys-org.description: A study published in the Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment (JSTAT), inspired by the behavior of bacterial colonies observed in previous experiments, uses mathematical models to describe the expansion of competing populations. The aim is to understand which factors determine the success of one population over another.

phys-org.title: Rideshare launches boost regional GDP and flexible jobs, study finds
phys-org.description: Ride-hailing has become a routine part of urban life in the United States, but its broader economic impacts have been difficult to measure. As Uber and Lyft expanded across hundreds of cities over the past decade, they promised more flexible work for drivers and convenience for passengers. Questions remained, however, about how these promises translated into measurable changes in local economies.

phys-org.title: Mom or not, caring for babies changes the brain
phys-org.description: Freeman Hrabowski Scholar Bianca Jones Marlin studies how caregiving takes shape in the brain and how some biological adaptations are passed to the next generation.

phys-org.title: A cooperative approach to reproductive success
phys-org.description: Fertilization is often imagined as a frantic race, with millions of sperm competing for a single prize. But new research by a team of evolutionary biologists from Syracuse University, the University of Siena in Italy and the University of Szeged in Hungary reveals a more surprising reality, where success can depend less on competition and more on cooperation.

phys-org.title: Newly unearthed mechanism that helps plants 'feel full' could help crops use fertilizer more efficiently
phys-org.description: New York University researchers have pinpointed the molecular players responsible for plants "feeling full" once they've taken up enough nitrogen—a finding that could help scientists develop plants that absorb more nitrogen from the soil and allow farmers to reduce environmentally and economically costly fertilizer applications.

phys-org.title: How simple amber lights could make nights safer for insects
phys-org.description: Approximately 40% of insect species worldwide are thought to be in decline and under threat of extinction. Among the key causes are habitat loss, pollution and climate change. Another threat is artificial light from sources like streetlights and security lamps. In new research published in the journal Biological Conservation, scientists say a simple change in artificial lighting could help reduce this particular threat.

phys-org.title: Climate change could dramatically reduce water flowing from the West's headwaters
phys-org.description: The small mountain streams that feed many of the West's rivers may face a much drier future. A new study led by NAU researchers found that groundwater-fed streamflow, known as base flow, has been steadily declining across headwater watersheds in the western United States since 1950 and could decrease by 45% to 65% by the end of this century if current climate trends continue.

phys-org.title: New microscopy method achieves angstrom-scale localization precision with one laser
phys-org.description: Researchers in the lab of Sam Peng, the Pfizer Inc.–Gerald Laubach Career Development Assistant Professor of Chemistry at MIT and a core institute member of the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, have developed a super-resolution imaging technology. It allows scientists to visualize molecular structures with angstrom-level localization precision—three orders of magnitude beyond the nanometer-scale limits of standard fluorescent dyes—while simplifying the imaging process.

phys-org.title: Antibiotic resistance is spreading through South Africa's water systems. This study explains how
phys-org.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is defined as the ability of disease-causing microorganisms to withstand treatments like antibiotics.

phys-org.title: Webb reveals warped structure in nearby TW Hydrae's protoplanetary disk
phys-org.description: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers obtained high-contrast coronagraphic images of the protoplanetary disk around the young, nearby star TW Hydrae. Results of the observational campaign, published July 27 on the preprint server arXiv, shed more light on the nature of this disk.

phys-org.title: Supergene solves evolutionary puzzle of mirror-image flowers
phys-org.description: The left-right asymmetry of South African butterfly lilies (genus Wachendorfia) has been regarded as a classic evolutionary puzzle for more than a century. Due to the mirror-image arrangement of the floral parts, the plants achieve efficient cross-pollination. The molecular basis of this arrangement has now been uncovered by an international team led by the University of Potsdam.

phys-org.title: Why some nitrogen-processing enzymes are more efficient than others
phys-org.description: Nitrogen gas is abundant in Earth's atmosphere, but most living organisms can't readily use it. Only a subset of microbes with enzymes known as nitrogenases can break nitrogen gas apart and convert it into ammonia.

proj-syn.title: This Time Could Be Different for Russia Sanctions
proj-syn.description: High inflation and interest rates are eating away at the foundations of the Russian economy and sapping its growth. By hitting its most important sectors, and its essential source of foreign hard cash, new US legislation would pile enormous pressure on the Kremlin just when it is urgently needed.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Energy Curse Is a Political Choice
proj-syn.description: It is no secret why African countries with large fossil-fuel reserves nonetheless have failed to reduce extreme poverty or provide reliable electricity to all households. Those in power have made a conscious choice to privilege hard-currency export revenues, some of which then finance elite consumption rather than public investment.

proj-syn.title: The EU’s Incredible Shrinking Banking Sector
proj-syn.description: At the start of the millennium, all five of the largest European banks had a higher market capitalization than the largest US bank. What explains the fact that a quarter-century later, the largest US bank has a higher capitalization than all five top EU banks combined, and how can European policymakers address this dramatic reversal?

proj-syn.title: AI Must Enlarge the Economy, Not Divide It
proj-syn.description: To unlock AI’s full economic potential, we must steer it toward expansion. That requires replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with those that reward augmentation and investment in human capability.

proj-syn.title: Silicon, Not Software, Will Decide the AI Race
proj-syn.description: The AI race is no longer just about building better models. As competition shifts from scientific discovery to deployment, success increasingly depends on computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure, and markets large enough to justify the enormous investments they require.

proj-syn.title: The Limits of Asia’s Two Major Growth Models
proj-syn.description: Data from a period in which both China and India pursued deliberate industrial policies show that neither country's development route is accessible to other countries. At best, their experience can alert policymakers to structural limitations and coordination problems that will require their own homegrown solutions.

proj-syn.title: The World Needs Compassionate AI
proj-syn.description: With AI having become the frontline of an intense global competition for economic and geopolitical power, speed is rewarded, scale is celebrated, and market dominance is prized above all else. Under such conditions, we risk forgetting the most important question: Whom is this intelligence ultimately meant to serve?

proj-syn.title: Trump’s New Tariffs Are an Opportunity to Fight Back
proj-syn.description: Once again, President Donald Trump is subverting domestic and international law in an effort to seize a larger fraction of global value and supply chains, and harming the US economy in the process. The longer that businesses and other governments avoid standing up to him, the greater the disaster that awaits us all.

proj-syn.title: Explaining China’s Industrial Competitiveness
proj-syn.description: External headwinds have not weakened China’s manufacturing competitiveness. That is because the Chinese economy combines an unusually large manufacturing base, deep supply chains, fast engineering feedback loops, and cutthroat domestic competition to create global powerhouses.

proj-syn.title: When Politicians Ignore Economic Expertise
proj-syn.description: As politicians encroach on areas that require technical knowledge, the risk of costly policy mistakes increases. The failures of Narendra Modi and Donald Trump show that when it comes to economic policymaking, political acumen is no substitute for a deep understanding of incentives, markets, and institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Beijing Model Meets the Brussels Effect
proj-syn.description: As Europe races to rebuild its industrial base, China is focusing more on influencing international standards and governance frameworks. The two powers are converging because neither can hope to claim a dominant position in the global energy transition by relying wholly on its traditional strengths.

proj-syn.title: The Mexican Government’s Economic Spin
proj-syn.description: By cherry-picking 12 data points that supposedly contradict top ratings agencies’ assessment of Mexico’s economy and fiscal outlook, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum recently presented a just-so story that should convince no one. A glimpse of what her list excludes makes that clear.

proj-syn.title: The Middle-Income Health Trap
proj-syn.description: Many countries that graduate from low- to middle-income status soon find themselves stuck in the position of being too rich to qualify for aid, too poor to secure reliable market-based financing, and too indebted to expand public-health spending. But it doesn't have to be this way.

proj-syn.title: Europe Is Fiddling While Rome Burns
proj-syn.description: Focusing only on emergency planning, disaster response, and recovery after each climate catastrophe is no longer enough in Europe. Policymakers urgently need to start mapping Europe’s long-term future, which will require a fundamental overhaul of its infrastructure, energy system, and major economic sectors.

proj-syn.title: Saving Democracy Requires Taxing Extreme Wealth
proj-syn.description: If lawmakers are serious about addressing the threat that dynastic wealth poses to American democracy, they can draw on considerable research that has gone into designing a wealth tax that avoids the pitfalls of other countries’ attempts. With the appearance of the world’s first trillionaire, there is no time to waste.

proj-syn.title: The AI Threat to Financial Stability
proj-syn.description: In episodes like the railroad boom and the dot-com bubble, creditors and shareholders were wiped out, because investment in a genuinely transformative technology outpaced any plausible near-term return. With the US financial system and asset markets having become a one-way bet on AI, such an outcome today could be catastrophic.
